title: Operation Crush: An Intel Story
coreMove: In a crisis, reduce the noise to one company-level fight and keep a clean path for bad news to correct the plan.
sourcePressure: Operation Crush shows Intel under competitive threat, rapidly rebooting priorities while field signals from people like Don Buckout and Casey Powell move upward.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not claim panic creates excellence or invent extra competitive battle scenes.

sourceAnchors.name: Operation Crush
sourceAnchors.detail: Intel faced a major competitive threat and top management rebooted priorities quickly around Operation Crush.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Operation Crush gave Intel one fight to win, which made every side project prove whether it helped the fight or got in the way.

sourceAnchors.name: Don Buckout and Casey Powell
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names Buckout and Powell as people able to surface field problems without retribution.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A crisis system only works if people like Don Buckout and Casey Powell can carry bad news upward before the plan hardens around a false story.

hook: A team discovers OKRs in a conference room and suddenly gets aligned
A dashboard glows on a Monday morning and reveals the truth
A leader writes a goal on a whiteboard and everyone understands
opening with Operation Crush: An Intel Story as a definition rather than a pressure
counterintuition: Measurement is not bureaucracy, it is clarity
Goals are not dreams, they are systems
Accountability is not punishment, it is ownership
Operation Crush is not a mindset, it is a system
tryThisNow: Set a timer and write three goals
Ask yourself what matters most right now
write one OKR without checking whether it changes behavior

home chore chart with vague family goals
